about: The `annual_report_catalogue` table, published whole. See /api/schema for its grain. This file is fy 2015 only.

provenance.warning: These figures cite a document not present in the document table, so no address can be given for them. Treat any figure resting on them as uncheckable.

rows.name: Table of contents
rows.what_it_is: The report's own index of sections and the page each starts on. Useful as a cross-check on what the year believed it contained -- it names 'Balance Sheet', 'General Funds Revenue Chart', 'FY 2016 Receipts', 'Special Revenue Funds', 'Capital Projects Fund', 'Trust Funds', 'Five Year Outstanding Debt', 'Debt Repayment Schedule', 'Collection of Taxes', 'Omnibus Budget FY 2016', 'Town & School Employee Compensation'.
rows.layout: single column, dotted-leader style, grouped under ALL-CAPS department headings
rows.notes: The TOC calls page 22 'FY 2016 Receipts' but the page itself is headed 'FY 2015 RECEIPTS - JUNE 2015'. Two sections are listed as 'NO REPORT' (Historical Commission, Veterans' Agent) -- an explicit record of an omission.

rows.name: In Memoriam notices
rows.what_it_is: Four obituary notices for residents who died in 2015, each naming the town roles they held.
rows.layout: four prose blocks, name and age as a heading line
rows.notes: Names ages exactly: Marion M. Benson, 83; August 'Gus' S. Misner, 78; Senator Mary Padula, 89; David M. Shea, 67. Padula served as Town Clerk/Tax Collector/Treasurer for 30 years; Shea served on the Board of Health for 30 years -- useful for dating officeholder history.

rows.name: Town profile facts
rows.what_it_is: A short fact block: year incorporated, registered voters, tax rate, form of government, meeting dates, area, road miles.
rows.layout: one label-value pair per line, all caps
rows.notes: Carries FY'15 TAX RATE-$18.32, REGISTERED VOTERS-7115, ROAD MILES- ABOUT 100, AREA- 26.63 SQUARE MILES. The DPW report on p56 separately says '86 miles of paved streets' -- two different road-mile figures in one document.

rows.name: Elected officials -- state and federal
rows.what_it_is: Contact directory for the Governor, Attorney General, congressional delegation and state legislators serving Lunenburg, with which precincts each state rep covers.
rows.layout: two-column, address blocks
rows.notes: Records precinct-to-state-rep mapping: 37th Middlesex = Precincts A, C, D; 3rd Worcester = Precinct B.

rows.name: Elected town officials with term-expiry years
rows.what_it_is: Every elected town board and its members, each with the year their term expires and the length of the term.
rows.columns: board (with term length) | member name | term expiry year
rows.layout: grouped list; board name as a heading with term length, then 'Name - YYYY' lines
rows.notes: Notes resignations and appointments-to-vacancy inline (e.g. 'Kirja Paananen-2016 (appointed to vacancy)'). Covers Assessors, Board of Health, Selectmen, Cemetery, Constable, Housing Authority, Library Trustees, Moderator, Park, Planning, School Committee, Sewer, Town Clerk, Trust Fund Commission.

rows.name: Appointed town officials
rows.what_it_is: Every appointed board, committee and single-officeholder position in the town, with members and term-expiry years.
rows.columns: committee or position (with term length) | member name | term expiry year or note
rows.layout: grouped list, sometimes two or three columns across the page for paired positions
rows.notes: Header reads 'TERMS ARE FOR ONE YEAR UNLESS OTHERWISE INDICATED.' Includes obscure statutory posts -- Clockwinders, Fence Viewers, Field Driver, Pound Keeper, Public Weighers (for P.J. Keating Co.), Dam Keeper, RACES Control Operator. Roles held by the same person across positions are visible (Kerry A. Lafleur is Hazardous Waste Coordinator and Hearings Officer).

rows.name: Combined balance sheet, all fund types
rows.printed_heading: TOWN OF LUNENBURG, MASSACHUSETTS / COMBINED BALANCE SHEET / ALL FUND TYPES AND ACCOUNT GROUPS / FOR THE YEAR ENDED JUNE 30, 2015
rows.what_it_is: The town's year-end balance sheet: assets, liabilities and fund equity, split across six fund columns.
rows.grain: one balance-sheet line item (per fund column)
rows.columns: (line label) | GENERAL FUND | SPECIAL REVENUE FUND | ENTERPRISE FUNDS | CAPITAL PROJECT FUND | FIDUCIARY FUND TYPES TRUST and AGENCY | ACCT. GROUP GENERAL LONG-TERM DEBT
rows.layout: matrix; column headers are stacked over three physical lines and OCR them out of order, so the header row must be reconstructed by position
rows.printed_total: TOTAL LIABILITIES/FUND EQUITY $6,574,503.35 $1,447,360.48 $7,287,364.36 $16,710,822.94 $2,397,564.62 $49,556,203 (matching TOTAL ASSETS on the same values)
rows.notes: Values are sparse -- most rows carry a figure in only one or two of the six columns, so column assignment cannot be inferred from order alone. Also prints TOTAL LIABILITIES and TOTAL FUND EQUITY subtotals. Real-estate receivables are broken out by levy year FY07-FY15, some negative.

rows.name: General fund revenue pie chart, FY15
rows.what_it_is: Pie chart of general fund revenue by source, as percentages.
rows.layout: pie chart; OCR recovers only scattered labels
rows.notes: Recoverable labels: PROPERTY TAXES 65.35%, STATE-LOCAL AID 23.56%, MOTOR VEHICLE EXCISE 4.61%, ALL OTHER 6.48%. Sums to 100.00%.

rows.name: FY2015 receipts by revenue source
rows.what_it_is: Every revenue line the town collected in FY2015, itemised, grouped by revenue class, with a summary block reconciling to a grand total.
rows.layout: three columns of label/amount pairs across the page, grouped under class headings (TAXES & EXCISES, INTEREST, DEMANDS, FEES, DEPARTMENTAL REVENUE, LICENSES/PERMITS, STATE REVENUE, FINES & FORFEITS, EARNINGS ON INVESTMENTS); the SUMMARY OF RECEIPTS block sits in the third column
rows.notes: The page heading is at the BOTTOM of the page (last line), not the top -- a heading-based search will miss it. The SUMMARY OF RECEIPTS block gives class subtotals: TAXES & EXCISES $22,402,150.73; FEES $544,131.63; LICENSES AND PERMITS $243,600.38; STATE REVENUE $7,501,423.18; SPECIAL ASSESSMENTS $56,055.11; FINES & FORFEITS $34,390.00; INVESTMENT INCOME $53,183.88; TRANSFER FROM OTHER FUNDS $838,054.00; NON RECURRING REVENUE $169,103.28. Contains CH 70 SCHOOL AID $5,605,872.00 and MSBA REIMB-SCHOOL $474,240.00. Reading order interleaves the three columns, so a naive line parse mixes unrelated sources.

rows.name: General fund expenditure pie chart, FY2015
rows.what_it_is: Pie chart of general fund spending by function, as percentages.
rows.layout: pie chart; OCR recovers scattered labels
rows.notes: Labels recovered: Education 54.97%, All Other 12.95%, Debt Service 9.30%, Protection 7.90%, General Govt Unclassified 6.57%, Department of Public Works 4.66%, General Government 3.66%. Percent-to-label pairing is uncertain from text alone -- the 6.57%/4.66%/3.66% figures print on a different line from their labels.

rows.name: General fund appropriations and expenditures by program
rows.printed_heading: TOWN OF LUNENBURG / GENERAL FUND APPROPRIATIONS / SUMMARY & CLASSIFICATION OF ACCOUNTS / FISCAL YEAR 2015
rows.what_it_is: The line-by-line general fund budget-to-actual for FY2015: what each department was appropriated, what carried forward, what it spent, what it encumbered and what returned to revenue. This is the town's appropriation ledger for the year.
rows.grain: one budget line (payroll / other expenses / etc.) within a department, with a bold subtotal row per department
rows.columns: PROGRAM NAME | APPROPRIATED | FUNDS FORWARD | TOTAL AVAILABLE | TOTAL EXPENDED | TOTAL ENCUMBERED | BALANCE TO REVENUE
rows.layout: repeating five-page table with the same 7-column header block reprinted on each page; sub-lines indented under a department, then an unlabelled department subtotal row; carry-forward amounts appear as a separate '$X fwd' annotation on the department's heading line rather than in a column
rows.notes: Columns are sparse -- most rows carry only 3 of the 6 numeric columns, so position, not order, determines which column a figure belongs to. Grouped under GENERAL GOVERNMENT, CENTRAL PURCHASING, PROTECTION, HEALTH AND SANITATION, DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC WORKS, SOLID WASTE/RECYCLING PROGRAM, FACILITIES & BUILDINGS, PUBLIC ASSISTANCE, SCHOOLS, LIBRARY, UNCLASSIFIED, DEBT AND INTEREST, STATE & COUNTY ASSESSMENTS, TRANSFERS TO OTHER FUNDS. School Department appears as two lines only (Payroll $11,364,548.00 / Other Expenses $5,390,115.00, total $16,754,663.00) -- no internal school detail. Monty Tech Assessment $760,058.00 is a separate line. State & County Assessments include Choice Tuitions $531,000.00 and Charter Tuitions $522,325.00.

rows.name: Special revenue funds -- balances, receipts and disbursements
rows.printed_heading: TOWN OF LUNENBURG / SPECIAL REVENUE FUNDS / FISCAL YEAR ENDING 6/30/15
rows.what_it_is: Every grant, gift, revolving and enterprise fund the town held: opening balance, receipts, disbursements and closing balance. This is where the money that does NOT appear in the general fund budget is recorded.
rows.columns: PROGRAM NAME | FORWARD 7/1/2014 | TOTAL RECEIPTS | TOTAL DISBURSEMENTS | BALANCE FWD 7/1/2015
rows.layout: five-page table, same header reprinted each page, grouped by GENERAL GOVERNMENT, SCHOOL DEPARTMENT, PUBLIC SAFETY, PARKS & RECREATION, HIGHWAY DEPT., COUNCIL ON AGING, LIBRARY, CEMETERIES, UNCLASSIFIED
rows.notes: This is the answer to the standing question about grants versus general fund. It names school grant funds individually with dollar flows: Title I #305, PL 94-142 #240, 50/50 Grant Sped Tuitions ($637,765.00 received / $644,776.54 disbursed), Full Day Kindergarten Grant, Teacher Quality, Race to the Top, Sped Program Improvement, Sped Early Childhood, Student Transportation Offset Fund. Also School Lunch, School Choice ($248,973.00 received), Chapter 658 School Athletics ($125,854.50 received / $113,962.65 disbursed), Extended Day Revolving, Non-Resident Tuition, School Facilities Use, After School Activities. Several funds carry NEGATIVE balances (Title I -$27,107.00; PL 94-142 -$51,747.42; 50/50 Sped -$119,894.01; Chapter 90 -$78,776.92). Rows with only one figure are dormant funds where forward = balance. The Water, Sewer and Solid Waste ENTERPRISE funds are listed inside this special-revenue table (p33) rather than separately.

rows.name: Capital project funds by authorising article
rows.what_it_is: Every open capital appropriation, keyed to the town meeting article that authorised it, showing what was appropriated or carried forward, what was spent/encumbered/transferred and what remains.
rows.grain: one capital project (or one item within an annual capital program)
rows.columns: ART #/YR | PURPOSE | APPROPRIATED FORWARD | EXPENDED/ENCUMBERED/TRANSFERRED | BALANCE
rows.layout: single page; annual capital programs appear as a heading row ('14 5/13 ATM FY14 Capital Program') with the individual items indented beneath, each item naming its department
rows.notes: Footnotes printed on the page: 'fwd - forward from FY 14', 'ATM - Annual Town Meeting', 'STM - Special Town Meeting'. Dominated by one line: '1 1/14 STM Construct Middle School/High School $61,100,887.00 fwd / $53,661,320.41 / $7,439,566.59'. Some expended figures are negative (credits back). Item names carry the owning department after a dash, which makes per-department capital spending recoverable.

rows.name: Assessments and revenues by major property class
rows.printed_heading: Fiscal 2015 Assessments and Revenues by Major Property Class
rows.what_it_is: The FY2015 tax levy split across the five statutory property classes, with each class's share of the levy, its assessed valuation and the resulting levy dollars.
rows.columns: Property Class | Levy Percent | Valuation by Class | Tax Rate | Tax Levy
rows.layout: five data rows plus a TOTALS row, at the top of the Board of Assessors page
rows.notes: A single tax rate ($18.32) applies to all classes -- Lunenburg does not split its rate. The Industrial valuation prints as '20,155.100' with a decimal point where a comma belongs (an OCR or typesetting error); the value should read 20,155,100 for the column to sum to the printed total.

rows.name: Valuation and tax history, nine years
rows.what_it_is: Nine consecutive fiscal years of tax rate, total valuation, number of accounts, tax levy and the year-over-year percent change in the levy.
rows.columns: Fiscal Year | Tax Rate | Total Valuation | Accounts | Tax Levy | Change (%)
rows.layout: nine rows, FY2015 back to FY2007, wide inconsistent whitespace between columns
rows.notes: Gives a nine-year levy series from a single page: 2015 18.32 / 1,146,501,536 / 5,062 / 21,003,908.13 / 3.5383 down to 2007 12.13 / 1,285,947,900 / 4,863 / 15,598,548.03 / 1.0643. Valuation FALLS from 2007 to 2011 while the levy rises -- the rate absorbs it.

rows.name: Abstract of assessments by property class code
rows.what_it_is: Parcel counts, total valuation and average value for each DOR property class code range -- the composition of the tax base.
rows.columns: Property Class Code/Description | Accts | Class Valuation | Avg.Value
rows.layout: twelve rows plus TOTALS, immediately under the valuation history
rows.notes: The printed TOTALS row omits an average-value total. Note the total valuation here (1,027,856,023) equals the RESIDENTIAL class valuation in the major-class table above, not the town-wide 1,146,501,536 -- the two tables total different universes and cannot be added together. Includes '600 - 821 Chapter 61, 61A, 61B 89 2,046,198 22,990' (agricultural/forest/recreational land).

rows.name: Assessor's overlay, exemptions and abatements, five years
rows.printed_heading: Assessor's Account for Exemptions and Abatements
rows.what_it_is: Five years of overlay account activity: overlay raised, deficits, charges against it, releases to surplus and the remaining balance.
rows.columns: Description | FY2015 | FY2014 | FY2013 | FY2012 | FY2011
rows.layout: five rows across five year-columns
rows.notes: One row label is stale: 'Charges to 6/30/2010' heads a column series running through FY2015 -- the label was not updated when the table was rolled forward.

rows.name: New growth revenue, nine years
rows.what_it_is: Nine years of new-growth added valuation, the rate applied, the resulting new revenue and its percent change.
rows.columns: Fiscal Year | Added Valuation | Tax Rate | New Revenues | Change (%)
rows.layout: nine rows at the foot of the assessors page, above the signature block
rows.notes: The tax rates in this table are OFF BY ONE YEAR against the valuation-history table on the same page: FY2015 new growth is shown at rate 17.99, which is the FY2014 rate. Either the new-growth rate is the prior-year rate by convention or the column is misaligned -- the page does not say which, and the two tables sit six inches apart.

rows.name: Treasurer's cash by bank account
rows.printed_heading: TOWN OF LUNENBURG / Treasurer's Cash as of 6/30/2015
rows.what_it_is: Every bank account and investment the Treasurer held at year end, by institution and purpose.
rows.layout: single label/amount list; the page heading prints at the BOTTOM of the page, after the total
rows.notes: The total line says '6/30/14' while the page heading says '6/30/2015' -- one of the two dates is wrong. Two $5,000,000.00 school-construction CDs (Century Bank, North Middlesex Savings) dominate the balance.

rows.name: Trust funds fund-balance reconciliation
rows.printed_heading: TOWN OF LUNENBURG TRUST FUNDS FY 2015 / FY-2015 FUND BALANCE RECONCILIATION
rows.what_it_is: Every named trust and stabilization fund the town holds, reconciled from beginning principal and earnings through contributions, disbursements and transfers to ending cash and market value.
rows.columns: ACCOUNT NUMBER | FUND NAME | FY 2015 BEGINNING PRINCIPAL | FY 2015 BEGINNING EARNINGS | FY 2015 CONTRIBUTE TO PRINCIPAL | FY 2015 EARNINGS | FY 2015 DISBURSE PRINCIPAL | FY 2015 TRANSFERS OF EARNINGS | FY 2015 ENDING CASH VALUE | FY 2015 UNREALIZED GAIN/LOSS | FY 2015 ENDING MARKET VALUE
rows.layout: a landscape table that the OCR has transposed: each printed COLUMN becomes one text line, with all ~25 fund values strung along it, and the fund names arrive as one long run-on line. Row/column association must be rebuilt by position within each line.
rows.printed_total: GRAND TOTALS (p40): FY 2015 BEGINNING PRINCIPAL $2,336,487.83; BEGINNING EARNINGS $167,412.53; TO PRINCIPAL $83,936.00; EARNINGS $25,676.53; DISBURSE PRINCIPAL ($7,871.14); TRANSFERS ($4,838.47); ENDING CASH $2,600,803.28; UNREALIZED GAIN/LOSS $17,739.69; MARKET VALUE $2,618,542.97
rows.notes: Grouped into CEMETERY FUNDS, CONSERVATION FUNDS, LIBRARY FUNDS, SCHOLARSHIP FUNDS, MISCELLANEOUS FUNDS, STABILIZATION FUNDS, each with its own SUBTOTALS row. Named funds include PERPETUAL CARE, CHESTER MOSSMAN TEEN CENTER, LUNENBURG ATHLETIC BOOSTER, BARTHOLOMEW STABILIZATION ($1,388,105.33), ZONING STABILIZATION ($227,542.95), ARTS LOTTERY, L.E.A.P. FUND. p40 contains only the grand-total column fragments -- the table's last page carries almost no fund rows.

rows.name: Five years outstanding debt
rows.printed_heading: FIVE YEARS OUTSTANDING DEBT / As of June 30, 2015
rows.what_it_is: Long-term and short-term debt outstanding at each of five year-ends, split by purpose and by whether the debt sits inside or outside the statutory general debt limit.
rows.layout: purpose rows under 'Within the General Debt Limit' and 'Outside the General Debt Limit', each with a total row, then short-term debt, then a combined total
rows.notes: Footnote printed on page: '(1)Principal amount only. Excludes lease and installment purchase obligations, overlapping debt and unfunded pension liability.' Debt more than doubles in one year -- Schools outside the general debt limit goes from blank to $29,605,000 as the MS/HS bonds are issued.

rows.name: Authorized unissued debt
rows.printed_heading: Authorized Unissued Debt and Prospective Financing
rows.what_it_is: Borrowing that town meeting has authorised but the town has not yet issued.
rows.layout: eleven rows at the foot of p41, amount first then purpose
rows.notes: Dominated by 'School Construction 43,264,346.00'. One row has a blank amount ('- Fire Equipement', misspelled in the source).

rows.name: Debt repayment schedule to FY2047
rows.what_it_is: Principal and interest due in every fiscal year from 2016 to 2047 on each individual outstanding debt issue, with per-year and per-issue totals.
rows.grain: one debt issue (three rows each: PRINCIPAL, INTEREST, TOTAL)
rows.layout: one very wide table split across two pages -- p42 carries fiscal years 2016-2032 (the heading is on p43, so p42 has no heading of its own beyond the year row), p43 carries 2033-2047 plus a TOTAL column
rows.printed_total: TOTAL DEBT (p43 final column) $72,756,968; GRAND TOTAL PRINCIPAL $49,556,201; GRAND TOTAL INTEREST $23,200,767
rows.notes: The two halves must be joined on issue name to reconstruct any issue's full schedule. Issues are named by borrowing programme, several with the same label: 'MASS WATER POOL 3/4/5/7/9/13/14' (asterisked), repeated 'MUNICIPAL PURPOSE' blocks, 'MUNICIPAL PURPOSE SEWER', 'MUNICIPAL PURPOSE WATER', and the two school bonds 'MS-HS CONSTRUCTION $9,000,000.00' and 'MS-HS CONSTRUCTION $20,605,000.00'. GRAND TOTAL PRINCIPAL $49,556,201 ties to the balance sheet's long-term debt $49,556,203 within $2. Some 'MASS WATER POOL 13' interest rows print $0 across every year.

rows.name: Collection of taxes -- receivables by levy year
rows.printed_heading: TOWN OF LUNENBURG / FY2015 COLLECTION OF TAXES / RECEIVABLES SUMMARY / JUNE 30, 2015
rows.what_it_is: For every tax type and every levy year still open, the movement from opening receivable through commitments, adjustments, refunds, payments, abatements and transfers to the closing balance.
rows.grain: one tax type and levy year (e.g. 'REAL ESTATE / LEVY OF 2009')
rows.columns: FISCAL YEAR | FORWARD | COMMITTMENTS | ADJUSTMENTS | REFUNDS | PAYMENTS | ABATEMENTS | TRANSFER | BALANCES
rows.layout: two pages; the header row prints at the top of p44 but the page TITLE prints at the bottom of p44; p45 continues with no header at all
rows.notes: Sparse -- most rows carry two or three of the eight numeric columns, so column identity depends on horizontal position. Sections: REAL ESTATE (levies 2007-2015), PERSONAL PROPERTY (levies 1998-2015), MOTOR VEHICLE EXCISE (levies 1997-2015), then on p45 OTHER EXCISE TAXES, SUPPLEMENTAL TAXES, TAX LIENS, FORECLOSURES, ROLLBACK, DEFERRED PROPERTY TAX, WATER and SEWER USER CHARGES, UTILITY LIENS ADDED TO TAXES, UNAPPORTIONED ASSESSMENTS (sewer/water/street/septic betterments), APPORTIONED ASSESSMENTS ADDED TO TAXES. Personal property receivables from 1998 are still on the books in 2015. Note the columns' header line prints 'COMMITTMENTS' with two Ts.

rows.name: Cemetery burials for the year
rows.printed_heading: CEMETERY COMMISSION (list introduced by 'The following is a list of persons who were buried this year.')
rows.what_it_is: Every burial in the town's two cemeteries during 2015, by month, with the deceased's age and which cemetery.
rows.columns: NAME | AGE | CEMETERY | NAME | AGE | CEMETERY
rows.layout: two side-by-side name/age/cemetery column pairs, grouped under month headings; the month headings for the left and right columns interleave in the text stream
rows.notes: Cemetery is coded N or S (North/South). An asterisk means cremation ('*Denotes Cremation'). Veterans are marked with a war ('Eino Ahokas WWII 95 N'). Month order is scrambled in the text stream because JANUARY and JULY head the two columns of the same physical row. The DPW report on p59 says the department supports 'on average, forty burials a year'.

rows.name: Council on Aging service statistics
rows.what_it_is: Counts of volunteers, volunteer hours, meals delivered, clients served and van rides for FY15, embedded in prose.
rows.layout: prose sentences, not a table
rows.printed_total: combined events and service statistics totaled 10,060 units with 827 participants
rows.notes: 41 volunteers contributing 2,587.25 hours; 4,898 Meals on Wheels to 50 clients; 3,169 rides to 62 clients on the senior van. These are the only per-service output counts anywhere in the report -- everything else is dollars.

rows.name: Public access cable FY15 line item expenses
rows.what_it_is: The public access channel's operating expenses for FY15 by line item.
rows.layout: eight rows plus TOTAL
rows.notes: Ties to the L.E.A.P. Fund row in the special revenue funds table (p33: forward $266,081.17, receipts $94,735.78, disbursements $94,846.84, balance $265,970.11) -- one of the few places in the report where two independently-prepared tables can be reconciled against each other.

rows.name: Public access cable revenue vs expenses and expense percentages
rows.printed_heading: FY15 EXPENSES BY PERCENTAGES / FY15 REVENUE vs EXPENSES
rows.what_it_is: A five-line reconciliation of the PAC fund (starting balance, revenue, subtotal, expenses, ending balance) plus a pie chart of the same expenses as percentages.
rows.grain: one reconciliation line / one expense category
rows.layout: reconciliation block, then a pie chart whose slice percentages print as bare numbers before the labelled legend
rows.notes: Percentages appear twice on the page -- once as unlabelled slice callouts (31%, 5%, 9%, 6%, 2%, 16%, 6%, 25%) and again in the labelled legend. Salaries 31%, New Equip 25%, Equip/Maint 16%.

rows.name: Senior property tax work-off programme statistics
rows.printed_heading: SENIOR PROPERTY TAX WORK-OFF PROGRAM / CALANDAR YEAR JANUARY 1, 2015 - NOVEMBER 1, 2015
rows.what_it_is: Participation figures and the programme's eligibility rules and rates, plus the list of departments that hosted participants.
rows.layout: prose plus two bulleted lists
rows.notes: Rate is $10/hour up to 100 hours for a maximum $1,000 abatement; nine residents participated, accumulating 865.5 hours. Income limits: $40,000 one-person / $60,000 two-person household. Seven departments hosted. Note the printed heading misspells 'CALANDAR'.

rows.name: Sewer system operating statistics
rows.what_it_is: Connection counts, billing, delinquencies, fee rates and grease-trap counts for the sewer system, in prose.
rows.layout: prose
rows.notes: 764 properties connected, 378 with access not connected, 36 new connections in FY15; $715,400 billed in quarterly sewer bills; $41,759 of prior-year delinquencies added to property tax bills; 19 grease trap establishments; 171 house-to-house I/I inspections; Sewer Bank Fee of $220 per bedroom on new connections; 81% of sewage discharged to Leominster, 19% to Fitchburg. The $715,400 billed does not equal the $719,626.93 SEWER USER CHARGES committed on p45 -- different quantities, close enough to be mistaken for each other.

rows.name: Nashoba environmental health department activity counts
rows.printed_heading: TOWN OF LUNENBURG / Environmental Health Department / Environmental Information Responses
rows.what_it_is: Counts of every environmental health action Nashoba performed for Lunenburg in the year -- inspections, permits, plan reviews, consultations -- each with an explanatory paragraph.
rows.layout: dotted-leader label followed by a count, then an explanatory paragraph; heavily indented, OCR'd in 'layout' mode on p77 and 'plain' on p78
rows.notes: Counts include Lunenburg Office (days) 80; Food Service Licenses & Inspections 49; Beach/Camp Inspections 23; Housing & Nuisance Investigations 38; Septic System Test Applications 78; Septic System Lot Tests 234; Septic System Plan Applications 78; Plan Reviews 76; Permit Applications new lots 32 / upgrades 33; Construction Inspections 110; Consultations 19; Well Permits 14; Water Quality/Well Consultations 14; Rabies Clinics - Animals Immunized 9. p76 separately states 98 Title 5 inspections were reviewed. The dotted leaders make the count run straight into the label.

rows.name: Nashoba nursing, community health and dental activity counts
rows.printed_heading: Nashoba Nursing Service & Hospice / Community Health Nursing / Dental Health Department
rows.what_it_is: Visit counts by service type, clinic and immunisation counts, communicable disease case counts by disease, and school dental programme participation.
rows.grain: one service type or one disease
rows.layout: dotted-leader label/count lines with explanatory paragraphs; the disease list is a bulleted label/count list
rows.notes: Nursing Visits 590; Home Health Aide Visits 247; Rehabilitative Therapy 360; Medical Social Service 44; Hospice Volunteer/Spiritual Care 13; 12 clinics; 85 health promotion visits; 106 flu shots. Disease counts by name: Anaplasmosis 1, Campylobacter 1, Haemophilus Influenzae 2, Hepatitis C 4, Influenza 13, Lyme Disease 6, Strep B 3, Salmonella 1, Shigellosis 1 -- these sum to 32, matching the printed 'Confirmed' figure. Dental: Students Eligible 351, Participating 185, Referred to Dentist 23, Number of Programs 10.

rows.name: Fire department call volume by type
rows.printed_heading: FIRE DEPARTMENT (introduced by 'In 2015 your Fire Department responded to 1985 calls for service, broken down as follows:')
rows.what_it_is: Calendar-2015 fire department response counts split into four categories.
rows.layout: two label/count pairs on each of two lines
rows.printed_total: 1985 calls for service (stated in the sentence above the breakdown)
rows.notes: Fires & Hazardous Conditions 483; Emergency Medical 967; Inspections 493; Other 37. These sum to 1,980, not the 1,985 stated -- the breakdown does not tie to its own printed total. Also states 5 career staff and 40-45 on-call, a 1.5% year-over-year increase and 5.5% EMS increase, and a 48% rise in call volume over 15 years.

rows.name: Fire department roster
rows.printed_heading: Roster of the Lunenburg Fire Department- 2015
rows.what_it_is: Every member of the fire department with their rank and certification level, flagged for specialised rescue team membership.
rows.layout: two columns of 'Name, Rank/Cert' entries
rows.notes: Footnote: '*Indicates member of Specialized Rescue Teams including Dive, Cave In and Confined Space Rescue Teams'. Certification suffixes (EMT, EMT-I, AEMT, Paramedic, Firefighter) are the only place in the report where staffing qualification is recorded.

rows.name: Police department roster by assignment
rows.printed_heading: POLICE DEPARTMENT / Lunenburg Police Department / 2015 Annual Report
rows.what_it_is: Police staff grouped by assignment -- administrative, patrol supervisors, detectives, community outreach, traffic/K-9, patrol officers, desk, reserve intermittent -- plus retirements and departures.
rows.layout: assignment headings with names beneath, some inline comma-separated

NOTE: the APD bylaw text appears TWICE (pp144-148 as Article 26's motion and pp149-153 as the amended version), and the Village Center parking and dimensional tables appear twice as well (p157 and p163) -- roughly ten pages of this section are a near-duplicate of another ten.

rows.name: FY2016 omnibus budget as voted
rows.what_it_is: The FY2016 operating budget as voted at the May 2015 annual town meeting, by numbered budget line, with departmental and grand totals. This is the appropriation the following year's report will show as spent.
rows.layout: TWO PAGES, each printed as two side-by-side halves, so the budget runs down the left half of p140, continues down the right half of p140, then the left half of p141, then the right half of p141. The OCR interleaves the two halves line by line, putting an unrelated account and figure on each physical line.
rows.notes: Line numbers run 1-82 and are the town's stable budget-line identifiers, referenced by later town meeting votes (the Nov 2015 STM on p180 amends 'Line 13, Reserve Fund', 'Line 75, Veterans' Benefits', 'Line 80, Monty Tech Assessment'). Section subtotals are printed: Total Maturing Debt $4,557,920.00; Total Gen Gov Unclassified $2,387,468.00; Total General Government $1,233,661.00; Total Central Purchasing 52,950.00; Total Protection $2,638,990.00; Total Health & Sanitation $66,663.00; Total DPW $1,467,738.00; Total Facilities & Buildings $625,370.00; Total Solid Waste/Recycling $147,000.00; Total Assistance $167,710.00; Total Schools $18,316,576.00; Total Library $363,849.00. School Department is line 79 at $17,399,092.00, Monty Tech Assessment line 80 at $801,484.00. The heading 'FY 2016 Omnibus Budget' prints only once, at the top left of p140; p141 carries no heading at all. Header column labels differ between the two halves of p140 ('VOTED FY 2015' on the left, 'VOTED FY 2016' on the right) -- one of them is a typo carried over from the previous year's layout.

rows.name: Special town meeting article votes, November 16, 2015

There are new class titles and some are renamed for clarity.' and '** New Grades have been assigned to those jobs mapped to the 2016 Salary Schedule. (revised Sept 2015)'. Grades run 1 (Library Page) to 18 (Land Use Director). Excludes elected positions, contractual employees, police below Chief, and all School Committee staff -- so it is not a complete town job list.

rows.name: Salary schedule for fiscal year 2016 -- HEADING ONLY, TABLE ABSENT
rows.printed_heading: TOWN OF LUNENBURG / SALARY SCHEDULE / FOR FISCAL YEAR 2016
rows.what_it_is: The heading and explanatory notes for the grade-by-step dollar salary schedule -- but the schedule itself does not appear. The page ends after three explanatory sentences about step increases and longevity.
rows.layout: heading and three note lines only; no grid, no dollar figures
rows.notes: This is a genuine omission, not an OCR failure -- p198 is 'plain' mode with 16 recovered lines and the next page (199) starts the next town meeting article. The document announces a salary schedule and does not print it. Notes that ARE printed: employees hired between 1 January and 30 June are not eligible for a step increase until the following 1 July; Step 1 covers the first 0-18 months; step increases run to 10 years, then a Longevity Bonus. Check whether the FY2016 report or an addendum carries the missing grid.

Several winners have implausibly low counts (George L. Emond Jr. elected on 14 votes). Two elected candidates are annotated 'Declined' (Wendy L. Bertrand for Sewer Commissioner, Paul F. Scheipers for the 3-year Park seat). One contest reads 'LIBRARY TRUSTEE - For 1 year / Vote for One  NONE'. Total ballots cast appear to be 247 across four precincts.

Department codes are free text and inconsistent: SCHOOL, POLICE, FIRE, DPW, COA, LIBRARY, ACCT, IT, PARK, CEMETERY, BUILDING, HEALTH, WIRING, PLUMB/GAS, LAND USE, PLANNING, SELECTMEN, REGISTRATIONS, TOWN MANAGER, VETERAN SERV, TAX WORKOFF. Selectmen appear at $100.00 each; the Superintendent at $136,578.97; the Town Manager appears twice under different names (LAFLEUR is absent, SPEIDEL KERRY TOWN MANAGER 130,102.20). Roughly 275 physical lines carrying two employees each. Compare to p24-28: this is what was PAID to people, while the appropriations table shows what was BUDGETED to lines -- the two are different universes and the report never reconciles them.
